recipes.name: Chicken with Quinoa and Veggies
ingredients_raw: 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into strips

steps.text: Bring chicken broth and quinoa to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook until broth is absorbed, quinoa is fluffy, and the white line is visible in the grain, about 12 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet. Cook and stir garlic scapes and onion in hot oil until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in chicken breast strips and cook until chicken is still slightly pink in the middle, about 5 more minutes. Remove chicken to a plate and set aside.

Pour remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in the skillet. Cook and stir zucchini and tomato in hot oil until zucchini is tender, 5 to 8 minutes. Return chicken to the skillet and sprinkle with feta cheese, basil leaves, and lime juice. Cook until chicken is fully cooked and hot, about 10 more minutes. Serve over hot quinoa.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken with Quinoa and Veggies
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breast meat, zucchini, tomato, fresh basil, and feta cheese make a delicious main dish when served over hot quinoa simmered in chicken broth.

video.description: Chicken strips, sauteed fresh veggies, and nutty quinoa are finished with feta and basil.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious! I substituted a number of things: shrimp for the chicken because I needed to use it up, broccoli for the zucchini, added 1 more tomato because they were on the small side, and mozzarella for the feta. I also didn't use the second 2 tablespoons of olive oil. And I used 2 garlic cloves minced. It only took me 45 minutes to get it on the table after receiving this recipe in my e-mail wondering what to cook for dinner. It was a lifesaver. My husband said it was as good as going out for a nice dinner. A very versatile recipe.

I threw in about a table spoon and a half of sundries tomatoes and it was delicious! The tomatoes alone were a little bland so I saw the need to add the sundrieds, small change but worth noting! Cook your veggies just how you like them. When you take the chicken out and set them aside, they continue to cook a little because of the heat they've retained. So throw them in after you've got your veggies just how you like them and then for the last 5-7 minutes or so, add chicken. It's already mostly cooked. (I sliced my chicken thin so it would cook faster)

My family loved it. I sauteed the onion and garlic together till they were almost translucent. then I added cubed yellow squash. When the squash was almost done I added cut up rotisserie chicken until it was warm. Then at the last I added the tomato and lime juice. I continued cooking on low until tomato was warm then served it over the quinoa. I added the feta cheese to my bowl while the rest of the family added Parmesan cheese to theirs.

LOVE this meal! I changed up a few thing and I must say it made a huge difference. I used two tomato’s, two zucc’s, and half white onion, half red onion, 5 cloves of garlic, and a red bell pepper. I used chicken thighs instead of breasts. The fat from them just makes it so much better. I also changed up the seasoning: salt, pepper, garlic pepper, garlic powder, paprika, turmeric, and red chili pepper flakes. I was afraid that this would take away from the flavor, but it only enhanced it!

Yum! A delicious and quick recipe with a good kick of tanginess. I omitted the lime in lieu of adding green tomato I needed to use up, which worked nicely. I also substituted 4 cloves garlic for the scapes, and it was not overly garlicky. For added color and nutrition, I mixed chopped kale into the hot quinoa to wilt. I used veggie stock instead of chicken broth, which resulted in bland quinoa, but mixing in the juices from the cooked chicken and zucchini fixed it.

I had a day-old rotisserie chicken in the fridge and was looking for a healthy side dish. I used what I had on hand for some substitutions and it turned out to be a great entrée! My other modifications: kale instead of zucchini, roma tomato (I'm not a huge tomato fan so the small one was perfect), and garlic cloves. I forgot to add the basil and it was still tasty! I added in the kale and chicken at the same time I put the tomato in. Pretty simple, healthy choice for dinner. I'll definitely be making it again.

This was a really great recipe. We were looking to eat seafood so I took the advice of another member and used shrimp and added mushrooms. I also turned this into a "bowl" by putting some baby spinach leaves into the bottom of each individual wide soup bowl then layering it with the quinoa and then the shrimp and veggies for serving. Delicious AND nutritious.

Mmmmm, loved this recipe! I especially loved the taste of quinoa cooked in chicken broth! I didn't use zucchini so it cut about 8 minutes off of my cook time. Instead of olive oil, I used coconut oil which makes the veggies and chicken just melt in your mouth. I didn't use any garlic either. I used red paper for some kick and chili powder, a pinch of Mrs. dash seasoning (no salt at all) onion, mushrooms, tomatoes, basil and cilantro....sautéed it for about five minutes, added the chicken, sautéed for another 5-10 minutes until chicken was done and then topped it off with a little goat cheese instead of feta and this dish had amazing flavor and it is better for you than the original dish! Delicious!

I always try to stick with the original recipe first time but I really wanted to make this and didn't have zucchini and had to look up what garlic scape was...not in season. So, I read a few other reviews and went with 2 garlic cloves and broccoli. I promise I'll try it in future as is but it turned out fantastic nonetheless. I would also agree with other reviewers that it comes together in 40 minutes or less if you don't want soggy vegetables. I'm going to make this recipe many times to add new variations to the vegetables like asparagus, snow peas, leeks, regular peas, sundried tomatoes, mushrooms, peppers, spinach and maybe a variety of fresh herbs out of my garden. Thanks Kmo for the basis to endless possibilities for a quick and healthy weeknight meal.

This is very good. There is way more quinoa that I find to be necessary though. Next time, I will cut that in half and stir it in instead of trying to use it as a base.
I made this a 2nd time, adding eggplant and cutting the amount of quinoa in half. It was much better.

I did broccoli instead of zucchini , lemon juice instead of lime juice and added a little turmeric for color and flavor. It was delicious and so light. Thanks for the recipe!
Love this recipe! Have made it twice. The second time my kids wanted Farro instead of Quinoa and it created quite a next texture. I also add Turmeric and Paprika as another cook recommended.
I added yellow zucchini and green zucchini. Used parsley because I did not have fresh basil. It was tasty and my family loved it. Lynnette G

I saved this as it was so delicious and I'll definitely want to make it again. Every bite has a new flavor. I made it as the recipe directs except only two tablespoons olive oil,4 cloves garlic instead of scapes and added seasonings. I used salt, pepper,garlic powder, paprika and turmeric.

Yes, I intend to make this again. I loved the taste. I did not have as much chicken so I was using less chicken and I increased the amount of zucchini. I added about a teaspoon of salt. I did not think it would turn out so great but it did.
This recipe was BURSTING with flavor! I fell in love!
This was so good. My husband and I both enjoyed it. This was my first time trying Quinoa.
I thought this was excellent. Next time I’m going to double the vegetables
